physiology:
The seat of this code is the throat, and the small gland wrapped around the front of it, the thyroid. The throat is the narrow place every word has to pass through, and the thyroid is the body's small pacemaker, the gland that decides how warm you are, how fast you move, how loud the engine of your metabolism runs underneath the day.

The shadow has a bodily floor here that is easy to miss. Intellect lives close to the throat. A clever mind keeps a tight grip on the muscles around the voice, on the breath just before a word, on the small hinge at the back of the tongue. Long years of arranging facts leave a person with a throat that knows how to defend a position and has forgotten how to say something simple and true. The thyroid feels it too, in its own way, the body running too hot or running flat, the pace never quite right.

The climb out is also bodily, and it is felt in the throat first. A loosening at the base of the neck. The breath dropping lower. Words coming with less padding around them. The voice begins to be used by something underneath the thinking, and the body recognises this immediately, before the mind has caught up. The code is seated where speech is made.
amino_acid:
Deeper than the throat, this code answers to a single amino acid, Tyrosine. Tyrosine is the raw material the thyroid uses to build the hormone that sets the pace of every cell in the body. Without it the gland has nothing to work with. The chemistry of speed, of warmth, of how quickly you metabolise the day, is built from this one small letter.

There is a teaching in that. The code that the traditions place at the throat, the code of facts and language and the long argument, is held up in the body by a substance whose first job is not to speak but to set the tempo of being alive. Before any word, the pace. Before the cleverness, the warmth. The body's wisdom is laid down beneath the talk.

The card asks for the same thing the chemistry already does. Let the pace come from underneath. Let the words be built on what is already keeping you alive, and they will land.
